Syntax & Toy Examples: Generating isolated, small C++ code snippets to learn C++ syntax. Debugging Assistance: Using GenAI to identify syntax errors, compiler errors, exceptions, or generic runtime errors in code that you have written yourself. Brainstorming & Design Discussion: Using GenAI to discuss high-level ideas. Complete or Partial Solution Generation: GenAI must not be used to generate the complete assignment solution or substantial portions of the C++ implementation. Core Data Structure Implementation: You must not use GenAI to design or generate the implementation of the required data structures. Core Algorithm & Program Logic Generation: You must not use GenAI to design, implement, or write the core algorithms, processing logic, workflows, or decision-making logic.
context: APU is introducing a Smart Campus Parcel Collection and Delivery Management System to manage the increasing number of parcels received for students and staff. The campus receives parcels from different delivery companies every day. Parcels may need to be received at the campus delivery centre, registered into the system, sorted for collection or delivery, assigned to collection counters or delivery personnel, collected by students or staff, and returned to the sender when necessary.

tasks.text: Task 1 – Parcel Intake, Sorting and Processing Module. This module manages parcels when they arrive at the campus delivery centre. It is responsible for registering parcels, maintaining their information, sorting them according to their next required action, and managing parcels waiting to be processed.

Task 2 – Parcel Service and Collection Management Module. After a parcel has been received and registered, it may require different services before the parcel process is completed. Examples include recipient collection, campus delivery, special handling, re-delivery and return to sender. This module manages service requests from creation until completion, cancellation or return.

Task 3 – Collection Counter and Delivery Resource Management Module. This module manages collection counters and delivery resources. It must manage resource availability and allocate parcels or service requests to appropriate resources while maintaining accurate resource information.

Task 4 – Parcel Activity and Record Management Module. This module maintains a history of important activities performed during parcel processing. It should allow staff to review what happened to a parcel and, where permitted, reverse an appropriate recent operation.

Task 5 – Parcel Category Organisation Module. This module manages the organization and retrieval of parcel information. It allows staff to organize parcel records according to a selected key and efficiently insert, search, display, update and remove parcel information.

selected_tasks.text:
Task 1 – Parcel Intake, Sorting and Processing Module
This module manages parcels when they arrive at the campus delivery centre. It is responsible for registering parcels, maintaining their information, sorting them according to their next required action, and managing parcels waiting to be processed.

Parcel Information
• Parcel ID
• Recipient ID
• Recipient Name
• Delivery Company
• Parcel Type
• Arrival Date/Time
• Parcel Status

Possible parcel types: Standard Parcel, Large Parcel, Fragile Parcel, Document and Special-Handling Parcel. Possible statuses include Received, Pending, Processing, Ready for Collection, Out for Delivery, Collected, Returned, Missing and Cancelled.

Functional Requirements
1. Register a New Parcel
Allow staff to register a parcel on arrival. Assign a unique Parcel ID, record recipient and delivery information, parcel type and arrival date/time, assign an initial status, and prevent incomplete or duplicate registration.

2. Maintain and Locate Parcel Records
Maintain registered parcel records and allow staff to display, search for and view selected parcels, including relevant details and current status.

3. Sort and Process Incoming Parcels
Classify and process incoming parcels according to their next required action. A parcel may be prepared for recipient collection, assigned for campus delivery, sent for special handling, processed for return to sender, or placed on hold for investigation. Update status and route the parcel to the appropriate next stage.

4. Update or Remove Parcel Records
Allow appropriate parcel information to be updated when circumstances change, including status changes, collection, delivery, return or cancellation. Invalid operations must be prevented.

5. Handle Exceptional Parcel Conditions
Handle duplicate Parcel IDs, invalid recipient information, missing parcel information, a parcel reported as missing, searching for a non-existent parcel, processing an already completed parcel, and attempting to process an empty collection.

Task 5 – Parcel Category Organisation Module
This module manages the organization and retrieval of parcel information. It allows staff to organize parcel records according to a selected key and efficiently insert, search, display, update and remove parcel information.

The team must select an appropriate organization key based on the requirements of the system. Possible organization keys include Parcel ID, Recipient ID, Delivery Company, Parcel Category or Service Type.

The selected data structure implementation must be meaningfully integrated into the parcel management system and must support the required operations.

Functional Requirements
1. Create and Maintain the Parcel Organization Structure
Allow staff to create and maintain the tree-based organization structure for parcel records. Each parcel record should contain sufficient information to identify the parcel and support the selected organization key.

2. Insert a New Parcel Record
Allow staff to insert a new parcel record into the selected data structure. The system should validate the parcel information and prevent invalid or duplicate records where the selected key requires uniqueness.

3. Search for a Parcel or Category
Allow staff to search for a specified parcel record or organization key. The system should display the relevant parcel information when the record is found and provide an appropriate message when the requested record does not exist.

4. Display and Traverse Parcel Records
Allow staff to display the stored parcel information using an appropriate traversal method. The team should select and implement a suitable traversal method based on the purpose of the operation. The team should explain why the selected traversal method is appropriate for the required output.

5. Update or Remove a Parcel Record
Allow authorized staff to update or remove a selected parcel record. The operation must maintain the properties and structure of the selected tree implementation.

6. Handle Exceptional Conditions
The system should handle appropriate exceptional conditions, including:
• Empty data structure
• Duplicate parcel or organization key
• Searching for a non-existent parcel
• Invalid Parcel ID or organization key
• Attempting to delete a non-existent record
• Attempting to update a non-existent record
• Invalid parcel information
• Removing a record that affects the data structure
